title: CEO & Founder
summary:
Zain Jeewanjee – Entrepreneur | Insurtech Pioneer | Investor | Speaker

Zain Jeewanjee is a seasoned entrepreneur, Insurtech pioneer, and investor with over four decades of experience in insurance, technology, and business innovation. A Silicon Valley veteran, he has been at the forefront of disrupting the insurance industry by developing cutting-edge solutions that transformed how policies are sold, managed, and distributed online.

In 1985, Zain created the first visitors’ medical insurance plan for travelers coming to the USA, laying the foundation for what is now a multi-billion-dollar industry. In 1997, he invented the first online policy issuance system, which became the backbone for MetLife’s travel insurance platform in 1999, enabling 30,000 agents to sell policies digitally. He also built the first online event liability insurance platform (OneDayEvent.com) and the first CRM platform designed specifically for insurance agents in 1999. Over the years, he has developed multiple Insurtech solutions that continue to shape the industry today.

Beyond his ventures, Zain is an active investor, advisor, and board member for multiple startups, helping businesses scale through strategic insights and innovation. He is a Charter Member of TiE Silicon Valley and was a founding team member of TiE Lahore and TiE Karachi, playing a key role in fostering entrepreneurship in Pakistan.

As a global speaker, Zain frequently shares his expertise on Insurtech, startups, and business growth at conferences worldwide. He remains deeply committed to education and philanthropy, supporting institutions like LUMS, Habib University, IBA, and TCF while actively mentoring the next generation of entrepreneurs.

Zain currently owns and operates multiple insurance companies and continues to push the boundaries of innovation in the industry.

summary:
🤖 Building Novolo



A Note to Novolo Employees, Stakeholders, and Partners:

It’s important to remember that we are in the early stages of exponential technological advancement. The pace will accelerate, the stakes will rise, and the landscape will become increasingly strange and controversial.

When I started building Novolo in 2021, people often asked me what AI was. That question doesn’t come up much anymore. Now, when I mention Novolo is an AI company, people usually look excited or like they want to punch me in the nose.

Many of us, myself included, have even begun receiving threats from anti-tech extremists. Expect this to grow.

The majority of these extremists have used the actions of certain governments and corporations to define the ethos of all tech companies. Many believe that, even with good intentions, individuals and organizations building technology of any kind are inevitably tied to ‘the system’ and are thus part of the problem. Obviously, I disagree with this sentiment.

I think it’s entirely possible for a business to build beneficial technology without killing whales or using ‘creative tax strategies,’ and Novolo will continue to do so. Unfortunately, the choices that other companies make will always warp the public’s perception of Novolo, no matter what we do ourselves.

Given the rampant ethics washing these days, it’s understandable when the public reacts skeptically when we and other tech companies claim to “build technology that will make the world a better place.”

Lucky for us, I believe the same technologies that will change people’s lives for the better will also change our bank accounts for the better.

We’re building technology to make the world a better place, and we’re trying to make money while we do it.

We’re not heroes, and we’re not villains.

Thomas Holt
Founder/CEO, Novolo
August 12th, 2024

title: CEO & Founder
summary:
Before starting Dost, I worked across engineering, sales, and business strategy. I started as a telecom engineer but quickly realized I didn’t want to spend my life behind a screen. I was more interested in solving real business problems.

That shift took me into project management, sales, and strategy roles at companies like Liberty Global, SAP, and Tech Data. Along the way, I worked closely with finance teams and saw a huge problem: industries like manufacturing, retail, and distribution were stuck with outdated financial processes.

Tech companies had modern finance tools. Everyone else was drowning in spreadsheets, slow approvals, and manual payments. CFOs wanted to be strategic, but their teams were buried in admin work.

That’s why I started Dost—to fix this. We help finance teams automate AP, payments, and reconciliation with AI so they can focus on making strategic business decisions. 

But building a company is about more than just solving a problem—it’s about building the right team. My leadership style is simple: ownership and execution. I don’t micromanage. I believe in giving people the space to take responsibility, make mistakes, and grow.

Outside of work, I’m big on discipline. I’ve played water polo since I was nine, and I still train regularly, swimming, lifting, and staying active. 

I also focus on mental clarity through meditation and structure.

If you’re a finance or operations leader tired of slow, outdated systems, let’s connect.
